summary.intent: Run an automated QA sweep agent (hackaton project) against the kutt URL shortener, triage its findings, and refine the sweep agent's prompt to reduce false 'broken' verdicts on time-dependent behavior.
summary.outcome: The kutt P1 run finished with 97 passed, 31 failed and 13 skipped across 15 files, and a report was written. A time-dependent-behavior rule was added to the sweep prompt and committed. The S-105 re-run still returned 'broken', so the rule's effect is unconfirmed.

repo: Sweep agent prompt lives in src/main/agent/sweep.ts; changes need a rebuild before re-running a scenario such as S-105 against kutt.
kutt runs locally on SQLite with migrations applied at startup, and a full P1 run takes about 1 hour.
kutt expired links are cleaned up by a cron job rather than at request time, so there is a window where expired links still redirect. This can make the sweep agent report false positives.
Findings from the kutt run: expired links still redirect, `data:` URLs are accepted as link targets (phishing risk), and deleting a domain with links=false still deletes its links (data loss).

code.finding: The sweep prompt now has a rule against marking time-dependent behavior (such as expiry cleanup) as 'broken'. The agent ignored it on re-run of S-105 and still reported 'broken'.

workflow: Long-running runs were monitored with repeated background Bash waits of about 10 minutes each.
Verify agent findings against source code before trusting them, for example by checking the cron schedule for the expired-link behavior.
Re-running a single scenario after a prompt change is a cheap way to test the change, but one run isn't enough to judge it.
